extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, trademark practitioners, OED counsel, and attorneys appearing in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural/merit criteria applied in USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline (OED) proceedings leading to default, findings of unauthorized practice, and imposition of sanctions (exclusion/suspension). Focuses on service, pleading, motion practice, practitioner eligibility, and sanctioning factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may serve a complaint by mailing a copy by 'Express Mail,' first-class mail, or any delivery service that provides ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery to the respondent at the address provided to OED pursuant to § 11.11, or if not registered, to the respondent's last address known to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service is accomplished when the complaint is mailed and delivered by first-class mail, return receipt requested, to the address provided pursuant to Rule 11.11; personal receipt by the respondent is not required for service to be complete, but evidence of personal delivery indicates personal knowledge. (Motion Ex. A; Tracking/return receipt evidence cited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify contact information (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered attorney or agent must notify the Director of his or her postal address for office, e-mail addresses, and business telephone number, and every change to any of said addresses or telephone numbers within thirty days of the date of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing and updating the address of record is the basis for proper service under Rule 11.35; failure to update can affect where service is effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer requirements and consequences of failure to answer (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(b)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An answer must be made in writing, filed with the hearing officer, and include a statement of the facts that constitute the grounds of defense and shall specifically admit or deny each allegation set forth in the complaint. Every allegation not denied is deemed admitted. Failure to timely file an answer constitutes an admission of the allegations and may result in entry of default judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines: complaint must state a time (not less than 30 days) for filing an answer. The Tribunal may extend deadlines, but if respondent does not file an answer that meets the Rules, respondent is in DEFAULT and admissions follow. (Explained and applied in default finding.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for motions and requests (37 C.F.R. § 11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions must comply with form and substance requirements set forth in Rule 11.43, including the requirement that the moving party confer with the opposing party prior to filing in a good faith effort to resolve the issue raised by motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that do not comply with 11.43 (procedural defects, failure to serve opposing counsel, failure to show good cause or to confer) may be denied and 'future submissions that do not conform to the formal requirements of the Rules may not be accepted.' (First Order; Third Order; orders denying extension requests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of motions/requests on opposing counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: All filings, motions, and requests should be served on counsel for the OED Director (and opposing parties) as required by the Rules; ex parte submissions to the Tribunal that are not served on the OED Director are procedurally defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's multiple facsimile requests were repeatedly not served on the OED Director, and therefore were procedurally deficient and were denied or forwarded ex parte by staff; failure to serve can justify denial of relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice / eligibility to practice (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.1, 11.14, 2.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an individual qualified to practice under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14 — generally an attorney in good standing of the highest court of any State — may represent an applicant, registrant, or party before the PTO in trademark or other non-patent matters; individuals not attorneys in good standing are not recognized to practice before the Office in such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practicing trademark/non-patent matters while not in good standing or in violation of a court order constitutes unauthorized practice and supports discipline/exclusion (applied to respondent's filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific disciplinary rule violations (37 C.F.R. part 10 citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of the PTO Disciplinary Rules can include: Rule 10.23(a) (falsely presenting oneself as authorized to practice before the PTO / engaging in unauthorized practice), Rule 10.23(b)(4) (falsely presenting authorization to practice in trademark matters), Rule 10.23(b)(5) (violating prior disciplinary order), and Rule 10.31(c) (holding oneself out to applicants as authorized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision identifies these rules as the bases for findings of misconduct where the respondent signed and filed multiple patent and trademark submissions while not authorized; the Order also notes a Count alleged under 10.23(b)(6) but found not proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default judgment effect (admissions and proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: By rule, an admission by default may be entered where respondent fails to timely file an answer; every allegation in the complaint not denied is deemed admitted and may be considered proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entry of default judgment admits allegations in the complaint only (not additional allegations in motions), and the Tribunal makes findings based on those admitted allegations. (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e) and related explanation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning considerations (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining sanctions, the Tribunal must consider: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to a client, the public, the legal system, or the profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused by the misconduct; and (4) the existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four listed considerations are applied to choose an appropriate sanction (here resulting in exclusion). The decision explains how each factor was weighed against respondent (duty breaches, intentional misconduct, potential for significant harm, presence of aggravating factors, absence of mitigating factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating/mitigating factors (ABA Standards and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggravating factors may include a prior disciplinary offense, a pattern of misconduct, multiple offenses, refusal to acknowledge wrongful nature of conduct, and substantial experience in the practice of law; mitigating factors may reduce sanction if present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director asserted several aggravators from the ABA Standards (2005); the Tribunal considered these and found no mitigating factors to apply in this case. Examples and case citations are used to justify exclusion when aggravators are present and misconduct is intentional/repetitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO and state disciplinary relationship; PTO authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action by the PTO does not preempt state regulation of the practice of law; nevertheless, the PTO has exclusive authority to suspend or exclude patent practitioners from practicing before the PTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited precedents (Kroll v. Finnerty; Sperry v. State of Florida) support concurrent but independent authority of state courts and the PTO; pendency of state action is not a bar to PTO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of remedy available to ALJ/Hearing Officer (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.39, 11.54(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer has delegated powers under Rule 11.39 to make initial decisions under Rule 11.54; Rule 11.54(a)(2) allows an initial decision to contain an order of default judgment, suspension, exclusion from practice, reprimand, or dismissal of the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribunal is constrained to the remedies authorized by those rules and will not grant additional relief beyond that authority; the decision applies that limitation in denying other relief beyond exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioners and reinstatement procedure (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded practitioners have duties set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, and petitions for reinstatement are governed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs respondent's attention to those provisions when exclusion is imposed; these provisions govern post-exclusion obligations and the process to seek reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of pleadings and submissions (conformity to Rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests, motions, and other submissions must meet the formal requirements of the Rules (form, substance, service). Submissions that are 'procedurally and substantively defective' do not satisfy the standards and may be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribunal repeatedly instructed respondent to 'familiarize himself with the Rules' and warned that future non-conforming submissions 'may not be accepted.' Multiple facsimile requests that lacked form, substance, and service were rejected as insufficient to avoid default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary facts and decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The facts and circumstances of disciplinary proceedings shall be fully published in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's official publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of the decision and facts is a routine consequence and part of disciplinary transparency; the Order states the decision will be published.
